answer: A stake-weighted reputation thread ties each agent's earnings to a locked deposit that only grows through verified work, so a fake identity starts at zero and must pay real cost to climb. A newcomer cannot fake history: every attestation is a public link in its record, and a Sybil splitting its stake across many identities dilutes each one's standing. The voyage from unknown to trusted is slow and expensive, since an attacker must fund the whole summit of fake reputations at once, while honest agents keep the rewards cheap copies cannot reach.
